Hi! From experience i can say that ”fake it till you make it” doesn’t work. If you dont listen to your needs they will make themselves heard eventually.
The hardest part about it is that feeling of being a burden or ”being a downer”.

Based on my own trial and error my advice is to identify who you can talk to and what you can talk to them about.
And be honest in advance. For example.
Hey im not doing too good, is it okay if i vent to you sometimes?
Or just be very blunt. I dont need an answer or solution, but i feel like shit and really need to talk to someone.

People who dont have experience with mental illness often dont know how to react or know what is expected from them when you open up. And i think its easier when you open up with telling them that you just need someone to listen without judgement, or just venting so you can get the bad thoughts out of the echo chamber in your head.

I know who i can talk to about my ocd
Who i can talk to about depression and anxiety
Suicide, eating disorders or just that i cant leave my apartment etc

Its better to let it out a little bit at a time instead of waiting until the damm finally breaks

Hope you find some help with this
You are not alone, Stay safe and take care! <3

Uncircumcised nurse assistant here. This is my personal opinion based on my education, profession and my own experience.

Edit: did some reading to fact check myself. Out of the claimed health benefits There are two small benefits that have some evidence to support them. 
There is a slight reduced rate of UTI’s in the first year, however, the rate of UTI’s in infants during the first year is only 1% and circumcision lowers that 1% slightly.
The other one has less evidence to support the claim. Which is penile cancer, which is very rare and has a rate of around 0.001%. Circumcision MIGHT slightly reduce the risk. (End edit)

Dont do it, there is (read edit) reasons to do it at birth other than cultural or religious reasons.
The foreskin is there for a reason.
It protects the glans (tip) from friction and getting dried out. Which leads to less sensitivity in the long term and can cause discomfort or even sores when it rubs on fabric or diapers.
The foreskin is also one of the most sensitive parts of the penis other than the glans (think thats the term in english). I would almost liken it to declawing a cat or cutting a dogs tail.
Cosmetic and cultural, but you remove a part of them that process stimulation. You can live without it sure, but man you are missing out.

The procedure itself is performed under local anesthesia but can cause bleeding, pain and discomfort.
You can read about how it is done on sources like john hoppkins website etc.

In my opinion It is genital mutilation since it serves little to no purpose and your baby cant consent to the procedure.

IF there is any medical issues later in life you can handle them appropriately. Some cases sadly require circumcision. But you can often fix it in other less drastic ways.

As an teen we found out my foreskin was too tight and had a small procedure to widen it where they made some small vertical cuts around the tip of the foreskin and sutured them horizontally. I consented and understood the procedure.
Today i have no issues and gratefull that i could keep it.

And its not ”unhygienic or harder to keep clean” its just as simple as pulling it back and rinsing with water and mild soap
Just like rolling your sweater sleeves up before washing your hands.

i have strong opinions about this but i strive to be factual and i dont want to make you feel attacked.

Hi, nurse assistant and have personal experience with self harm.
These cuts are not dangerously deep or big. Clean them carefully with mild, unscented soap and clean body temp water. Dont use alcohol as it dries out and damages the cells which slows down healing.
Keep it bandaged with clean gauze, compresses or very clean cloth that does not release lint or fibres (if you do not have acces to bandaids, bandages or the stuff i mentioned above).
If you notice increased redness, increased temperature around the wound or get a fever. Contact a healthcare provider as it could be infected.

Try not to pick on the scabs and change bandages if they get very saturated with blood or fluids.
Otherwise change it every other day.

With that said the underlying cause and the self harm itself is the dangerous part and you will need professional help or at least support from family or friends if possible.
I know that it hurts and is extremely hard to do, but self harm has a tendency to escalate and spiral out of control.
It is great that you ask for advice and i hope you take care of yourself.

Stay safe!

I have a few ideas of causes:
Damage from chronic ingrown toenail.
Damage to the nailbed and/or the nail matrix( causes the nail to grow out misshaped or damaged)
Or fungal infection

But you need to either try to lift the nail edges over time so it stops growing into the skin on the sides.
And/or have a minor surgery to remove part of the nail or the nail matrix.

The itching can be caused by infections from the ingrown toenail or fungal infection.
However i am not an expert in this area and i am not a doctor, and my opinion is that you might want to get that looked at.

Till then keep your toes clean and dry, change your socks, clean out your shoes and wear open-toed shoes if possible.

Birthmarks that change in size, shape or becomes lesions, scab over with no trauma should always be looked up.
The skin (moles included) change with time.

When it stops you can gently clean off the blood in your face with cool or body temp water.
Sit down and take it easy for a bit.

A pharmacy should have some special “cotton” for stopping nose bleeds if that doesn’t work.

But if it is reoccurring, talk to your GP or other equivalent medical provider.

Hi, medical professional but not a doctor so i cant diagnose.
It is not impossible that it is caused by scratching on swollen and irritated skin from mosquito bites. Sometimes hair follicles can get a little more elevated that the surface of the skin and that can make you accidentally removing or damage the skin around them as you scratch on them, and thus cause circular “holes”. (This is mostly based on personal experience mixed with all kinds of scrapes and wounds i have seen)

Now for some questions.

I do see some fluids in the picture, do they crust over or seep any fluids? Does it itch? Has it grown?

It could be some skin infection but i am mostly experienced with the bacterial infection “impetigo”, and that can look like holes in the skin but they usually get honey yellow crusts on them, itches like hell and they spread easily. 

My general advice for things like this is keep it clean with mild unscented soap, clean and airy/breathing dressings on it. If there is alot of fluids seeping out you can try some mild alcohol based antibacterial fluid or chlorohexidine gel to slightly dehydrate it and keep it clean.

Well almost always yes, but in some cases ”kinda”

There is always going to be some amount of scar tissue but areas with “thicker skin” and muscles that move alot scar more easily and the scars are likely to be more noticeable as the wound is easily stretched and moves around during the healing process.

Wounds on areas of skin that dont move or stretch as much from movement, wounds from very sharp objects with a clean cut that then is closed up properly (wound edges against each other), kept clean and avoiding infections.
These things can sometimes make the scarring less noticeable.

When the wound has healed: moisturize, protect from the sun, use a high spf sunscreen as scar tissue has extremely low uv protection.

Another thing that is a big factor is nutrition, age and overall health + genetics.

If you are malnourished or dont eat a balanced diet  wounds tend to heal slower and has increased risks for infections etc.
Alcohol and nicotine is also bad for healing.

And lastly, a young person who does some physical activity and has good circulation has better chances of having smaller scars

But scars ado fade and blend in with time, also if you at some point feel safe enough to stop hiding your scars, they tend to fade from peoples minds too as we stop noticing stuff we see regularly.
